title: User Input / Output
subStepTitle: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
intro: Reading input and writing output cleanly is the first skill that separates “I know syntax” from “I can ship solutions.” In User Input / Output, treat stdin/stdout as a contract: know the types, the separators, and when to flush. Classic framing from the roadmap note “c basic input output”.
intuition: Think of the judge as a pipe: your program consumes tokens and emits a deterministic answer. Match the sample format exactly.
approach: Identify how many values and their types from the statement.
Read with the idiomatic API (cin/scanf, Scanner, input(), fmt.Scan).

cpp.notes: Prefer \n over endl unless you need a flush.

java.notes: Scanner is fine for learning; BufferedReader for tight TL.

python.code:
a = int(input())
s = input().strip()
print(a, s)
python.notes: input() is enough for most beginner tasks.

go.code:
package main
import "fmt"
func main() {
    var a int
    var s string
    fmt.Scan(&a, &s)
    fmt.Println(a, s)
}
